definitions.explanation: Describes something that applies broadly or comprehensively rather than to specific parts. Often used when summarizing or giving an overall assessment.

examples.japanese: {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に{良|よ}い{結果|けっか}だった。
{全般的|ぜんぱんてき}な{傾向|けいこう}として、{売|う}り{上|あ}げは{伸|の}びている。
examples.english: As a general trend, sales are growing.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}のテストは{全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に{難易度|なんいど}が{高|たか}かったと{思|おも}います。
examples.english: I think this test was difficult across the board.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a na-adjective modifier ({全般的|ぜんぱんてき}な + noun) or as an adverb ({全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に). The adverbial form {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に is particularly common in writing and formal speech to introduce overall assessments.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}な{評価|ひょうか} (overall evaluation)
- {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}に{見|み}て (looking at it overall)
- {全般的|ぜんぱんてき}な{傾向|けいこう} (general trend)

SIMILAR WORDS:
Compare with {全体的|ぜんたいてき} (as a whole), which emphasizes the whole as a single unit, while {全般的|ぜんぱんてき} emphasizes breadth across various aspects or areas.
